hook.text: A V8 cruising on a highway doesn't need all eight cylinders—half are doing nothing useful.

buildup.text: Running all cylinders at light load wastes fuel because each pumps air it can't fully use.

discovery.text: Cylinder deactivation shuts half the cylinders, closing their valves and cutting fuel delivery.

twist.text: The engine switches between four and eight cylinders so smoothly most drivers never notice.

climax.text: GM's Active Fuel Management saves up to 8 percent on highway fuel consumption.

punchline.text: Half the cylinders nap while the other half work harder.

quiz.question: What does cylinder deactivation do at light engine loads?
options: Shuts down some cylinders to save fuel
